answer: Escrowed identity deposits make sybil attacks costly: each new agent locks a bond in a shared vault before it can transact. Vouching peers co-sign and share slashing risk, so fake identities cannot sit on a flat mesa of free entry but must climb an eroded karst where every forged clone forfeits real capital. Spinning up 1,000 sybils means funding 1,000 bonds, and any detected collusion burns them all at once.
